title: ‘We Are Horrified’: Academic Freedom at Risk With Uzbek Professor’s Arrest in Kazakhstan
gist: An Uzbek international-relations professor at Maksut Narikbayev University in Astana was secretly detained on espionage allegations for nearly two months before BBC Uzbek broke the story, and the university has already distanced itself from him, with both Kazakh and Uzbek authorities refusing comment.

insights.claim: Dr. Ikboljon Qoraboyev, a 46-year-old Uzbek international relations professor at Maksut Narikbayev University (MNU) in Astana, Kazakhstan, was arrested on espionage allegations roughly two months before the case became public in late August.
insights.speaker: Catherine Putz
insights.so_what: Signals rising state security scrutiny of foreign academics in Kazakhstan, a risk factor for cross-border education/research partnerships and Western or regional institutions operating there.
insights.quote: an Uzbek professor working in Kazakhstan had been arrested nearly two months prior on allegations of espionage

insights.claim: Both Kazakh and Uzbek government authorities refused to answer media questions about the detention, and independent outlet Vlast could not get official confirmation of the case's basis.
insights.speaker: Catherine Putz
insights.so_what: A pattern of official silence around detentions of academics/foreign nationals is a governance opacity signal relevant to sovereign and institutional risk assessments in Central Asia.
insights.locator: paragraph on media questions to authorities

insights.claim: When asked about Qoraboyev's status, Maksut Narikbayev University immediately distanced itself, stating he 'is not currently a professor at the university' and redirecting inquiries to unnamed 'competent authorities.'
insights.speaker: Catherine Putz
insights.so_what: Institutional disavowal on state-security matters is a recurring pattern worth tracking for how universities and firms operating in authoritarian-leaning states manage political risk to staff.
insights.quote: is not currently a professor at the university. For any further information concerning his detention, please refer to the relevant competent authorities.

insights.claim: Qoraboyev had active academic ties to China through a China-Central Asia relations roundtable co-hosted with Fudan University's Center for Russian and Central Asian Studies just months before his arrest.
insights.speaker: Catherine Putz
insights.so_what: Worth watching whether China-linked academic exchange becomes a flashpoint for security suspicion in Kazakhstan, which could chill Sino-Central Asian institutional cooperation.
